note: The human half of §12.4's overlay: why a source path the plan never named is nevertheless inside its epic's scope. Keyed `<epic> <path>`. Entries marked HOT ZONE touch a file §2.D lists as shared, and the delegate reads those individually rather than accepting the sentence.

reasons.P1-02 packages/host/plugin-inventory/src: The consumer that reads recorded provenance in production. must[2] is about verification reaching a real inventory, and the inventory is where that call site lives.
reasons.P1-02 packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/i: HOT ZONE. Written from `git show 05c22146ef -- packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/index.ts` (+42/-1): `createTrustKernel` takes a new `config: TrustKernelConfig` carrying `trustAnchors`, a module-private `CONFIGURED_ANCHORS` WeakMap keyed by the handle holds them, and `configuredTrustAnchors` is a new export. That is a change to construction, not a read of it. The WeakMap keying is the load-bearing part: only a caller already holding the unforgeable handle can read the anchors, and a forged object reaches nothing because it was never a key. `createTrustKernel` still performs no I/O — the boot path reads configuration and passes the result — so the constructor stays total. An earlier version of this entry said P1-02 only READS `signatureRoots` and does not change construction, which was simply false.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/ca: Candidate-lock construction, which is half of must[0]: a lock that pins integrity has to be built somewhere, and the registry declared only the comparison side.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/co: The atomic commit path. must[0] requires the lock to be written durably; the registry named the decision functions and not the write.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/ga: The boot-admission decision the U stage proves. The registry declared the lock package broadly and this file is where admission is decided.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/lo: Created by this epic to close BLOCKED-135: real integrity read from pnpm-lock.yaml, replacing a `dsh.provenance.integrity` field nothing wrote. The plan predates the finding, so it could not have named the file.
reasons.P1-03 scripts/first100/verify-boot-path-: The structural gate §12.1 substituted for the withdrawn fetch-spy assertion: the boot closure contains no HTTP client. It is program infrastructure the epic was told to build, not product code.

reasons.P1-07 packages/workspace/workspace-trust: The local trust store the decision reads. The registry declared the policy and not the store it consults.
reasons.P1-08 apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts: HOT ZONE. Written from `git show c3992e5124 -- apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts` (+52/-3): profile boot imports `negotiateProfileLayerCompatibility` and `DSH_RUNTIME_API_VERSION`, runs the negotiation on the admitted layers before any patch reaches `boot()`, and the result gains a `compatBlockedLayers` field whose layers are absent from `bundlePatches` — so a blocked layer's plugin code never mounts (acceptance[1]). The change is an added step in the boot sequence, not a change to what boot already did. It is in this epic's scope because the clause is about boot ADMISSION: proving it in the solver alone would leave the refusal unreached by any launch.

reasons.P2-01 packages/identity/principal/src/in: The published ./invariant companion for the principal package, required beside the module it observes.
reasons.P2-02 packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/i: HOT ZONE. Written from `git show 1ac2dfe4d1 -- packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/index.ts` (+31/-5): the module imports `generateKeyPairSync`/`sign`/`verify` from node:crypto, mints an Ed25519 keypair per kernel, and holds it in a module-private WeakMap keyed by the handle — so the PRIVATE key is never a property of `signatureRoots`, which crosses the plugin boundary. `signWithSignatureRoots`/`verifyWithSignatureRoots` are new exports, and a handle this module did not mint is refused rather than handed an empty signature. This replaced a four-byte constant that was identical in every installation, so any deployment's token verified anywhere and verification could not fail (P2-02 must[1]). Construction changed here under P2-02's acceptance lock, and the lift records the same facts.
reasons.P2-03 packages/core/session/src/index.ts: HOT ZONE. Written from `git show ed09684ecf -- packages/core/session/src/index.ts` (+24/-0): the Session log gains a private `typeCounts` Map, maintained on every append, and a public `countEventsOfType(type)` reading it. Why: must[1] needs the manifest `sequence` to be one running position across two call sites (the native tool path and the PTC code-mode sub-dispatch), and a per-append counter avoids the O(n) scan a hot path would pay per operation. The method is deliberately generic — this Session names no manifest — because the event map is merge-extended downstream and a manifest-specific counter here would invert that dependency. An earlier version of this entry said the epic "contributes an event type and does not change the log itself", which described the declaration merging in dsh-action-manifest and hid this file's actual change.

reasons.P2-03 packages/action/action-manifest/sr: Created by this epic under §12.11: the actor resolution and the idempotency-key derivation both execution paths need. Not a hot zone — a new file in the package that already owns the manifest — but recorded because the plan named neither. It exists rather than living in each caller for the reason BLOCKED-136 measures: two paths deriving the same key is one rule with two implementations, and the derivation IS the contract (a replayed attempt keys the same, a new one does not).
reasons.P4-07 packages/workflow/workflow-worker-: Created by this epic in the U rebuild (§12.15-2): the run-side view of a lease — acquire, renew, and may-I-write. It exists rather than living inline in `host.ts` so `mayWrite` reads through the lease package’s own `checkFencing` instead of comparing epochs again; a second implementation of "is this token current" would be BLOCKED-136’s shape on the check that decides whether a stale worker may write.
reasons.P4-07 packages/workflow/workflow/src/ind: Two additions to `WorkflowErrorCode`: `LEASE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` and `RUN_HELD_BY_ANOTHER_HOST`. No existing member changed. They belong to the seam DEFINITION rather than to the worker-thread provider because the code union is the seam vocabulary — a provider inventing its own codes would make the seam callers switch on strings the definition does not know — and acceptance[2] needs a caller to tell a store outage from an ordinary refusal, which an untyped throw cannot carry. NOT labelled HOT ZONE: an earlier draft was, and the citation gate refused it for naming `HEAD` rather than a sha. Checking rather than arguing with my own gate: this file is not on §2.D hot-zone list (P3-01, P3-05, P3-07, P5-05, P5-06), so the label was over-classification, and a label applied outside its defined set makes the five that carry it mean less.
reasons.P4-07 packages/workflow/workflow-worker-: The engine plugin, where the lease is ACQUIRED — before the worker thread exists. Acquiring after the thread starts would leave a window in which two hosts both run the script, and no later fencing check undoes it: a refused write does not un-send what the worker already did. The heartbeat and the write guard deliberately do NOT live here; gate (u) refused an earlier version that put them in the plugin, and it was right on the design too, since the lease lifetime is the run lifetime. `leaseMs`/`heartbeatMs` are Config fields added in the same change.
